(a)

        (1) 
Subsection (a)(1) of section 314 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 246, as amended by section 3 of the Comprehensive Health Planning and Public Health Services Amendments of 1966, Public Law 89–749) is amended (1) by striking out “1968” the first time it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “1970” and (2) by striking out “and $5,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968” and inserting in lieu thereof “$7,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968, $10,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1969, and $15,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1970”.
 
        (2) 
Subsection (a)(2) of such section is amended by redesignating subparagraphs (I) and (J) as subparagraphs (J) and (K), respectively, and by inserting after subparagraph (H) the following new paragraph:


“(I) 
effective July 1, 1968, (i) provide for assisting each health care facility in the State to develop a program for capital expenditures for replacement, modernization, and expansion which is consistent with an overall State plan developed in accordance with criteria established by the Secretary after consultation with the State which will meet the needs of the State for health care facilities, equipment, and services without duplication and otherwise in the most efficient and economical manner, and (ii) provide that the State agency furnishing such assistance will periodically review the program (developed pursuant to clause (i)) of each health care facility in the State and recommend appropriate modification thereof;”.



 
        (3) 
The last sentence of subsection (a)(4) of such section is amended by inserting before the period at the end thereof except that in the case of the allotments for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1970, it shall not exceed 75 per centum of such cost ’.
  
    (b)

        (1) 
Subsection (b) of such section is amended by striking out “1968” the first time it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “1970” and by striking out “and $7,500,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968”, and inserting in lieu thereof “$7,500,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968, $10,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1969, and $15,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1970”.
 
        (2) 
Such subsection (b) is further amended by inserting immediately after “project grants to any other public or nonprofit private agency or organization” the following: “(but with appropriate representation of the interests of local government where the recipient of the grant is not a local government or combination thereof or an agency of such government or combination)”.
  
    (c) 
Subsection (c) of such section is amended by striking out “1968” the first time it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “1970” and by striking out “and $2,500,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968” and inserting in lieu thereof “$2,500,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968, $5,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1969, and $7,500,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1970”.
 
    (d)
        (1) 
Subsection (d)(1) of such section is amended by striking out “$62,500,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968,” and inserting in lieu thereof “$70,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968, $90,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1969, and $100,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1970,”.
 
        (2) 
Effective July 1, 1968, subsection (d)(5) of such section is amended by inserting “the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands,” after “American Samoa,”.
 
        (3) Subsection (d)(7) of such section is amended by adding at the end thereof the following new sentence: “Effective with respect to allotments under this subsection for fiscal years ending after June 30, 1968, at least 70 per centum of such amount reserved for mental health services and at least 70 per centum of the remainder of a States allotment under this subsection shall be available only for the provision under the State plan of services in communities of the State.”
  
    (e) Subsection (e) of such section is amended by striking out “$62,500,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968,” and inserting in lieu thereof “$90,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968, $95,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1969, and $80,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1970,”.
 
    (f) Effective July 1, 1968, subsection (g)(4)(B) of such section is amended by inserting “the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands,” after “American Samoa,”.
 
    (g) Effective July 1, 1967, subsection (c) of section 309 of such Act (42 U.S.C. 242g(c)), as amended by section 4 of the Comprehensive Health Planning and Public Health Services Amendments of 1966 (Public Law 89–749), is amended by striking out “each” after “$5,000,000” and by inserting after “the fiscal year ending June 30, 1968,” the following: “$6,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1969, and $7,000,000 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1970,”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this section only adjusts appropriation amounts and state-plan conditions for grants, which would not be participation. However, new subparagraph (I) requires the Secretary, a federal official, to establish criteria for state plans only after consulting with the State, an entity outside the federal government. That is consultation with an outside party before a federal decision, which meets the definition.
fable.s: criteria established by the Secretary after consultation with the State

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary to establish criteria 'after consultation with the State'. Since the State is an entity outside the federal government, and the consultation occurs before the Secretary makes the decision to establish the criteria, this constitutes participation as defined.
qwen_block.s: criteria established by the Secretary after consultation with the State
qwen_block.b:
1. **Think briefly**: The section contains the phrase "criteria established by the Secretary after consultation with the State". The tempting reading is "Yes" because it involves consultation with a State (an outside entity). However, the context is that the Secretary establishes criteria for a State plan. The definition states that participation involves consulting with people outside the government *before making a decision*. Here, the Secretary is making a decision (establishing criteria) and consulting with the State. This fits the definition of participation: "consultation or coordination with states... before a federal action". Wait, let's look closer. Is the "consultation with the State" part of the decision-making process for the *criteria*? Yes. The Secretary establishes criteria *after* consultation. This is a federal decision (establishing criteria) involving an outside party (the State). Therefore, it is participation.

Let's double-check against the "No" traps. Is it an application for a grant? No, it's about establishing criteria. Is it intra-governmental? No, the State is outside. Is it a report to Congress? No.

The key span is: "criteria established by the Secretary after consultation with the State". This explicitly requires the Secretary (federal) to consult with the State (outside) before establishing the criteria (a federal decision/action).

opus.w: The Secretary, a federal official, must consult with the State before setting the criteria for state health facility plans. A state is outside the federal government, so this is consultation before a federal decision. The tempting reading treats the section as only a grant and appropriations amendment, or as a state's own planning process. But setting the criteria is a federal action that requires outside consultation, so this is participation.
opus.s: consistent with an overall State plan developed in accordance with criteria established by the Secretary after consultation with the State
opus.b:
1. **Tempting wrong reading:** This looks like a grant and appropriations amendment. Most of it changes dollar amounts and how states build their own plans, which would point to "No." It also mentions "appropriate representation of the interests of local government" among grant recipients. That is a condition on who gets a grant, not participation in a federal decision.

2. **Why the answer is still Yes:** New subparagraph (I) requires the Secretary to set the criteria for state plans "after consultation with the State." Setting those criteria is a federal decision, and the State is outside the federal government. So an outside party must be consulted before the federal decision is made.

qwen_chat.w: The consultation mentioned is between the Secretary and the State regarding the development of a State plan for capital expenditures. This is part of the process for states to receive federal project grants. The definition explicitly states that participation 'does not include applications for benefits or grants.' Since the consultation is tied to the development of a plan for grant eligibility/funding, it falls under the exclusion for grant applications rather than constituting participation in a federal decision.
qwen_chat.s: provide for assisting each health care facility in the State to develop a program for capital expenditures for replacement, modernization, and expansion which is consistent with an overall State plan developed in accordance with criteria established by the Secretary after consultation with the State
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: The text mentions "consultation with the State" in subsection (a)(2), which might suggest participation because states are outside the federal government. However, this consultation is part of the process for a state to develop its own plan to receive federal grants. The definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants." The state is applying for/developing a plan to get funding, not participating in a federal decision-making process in the sense of advising or coordinating on a federal policy before it is made. The consultation is a procedural requirement for the grant application/plan development, not a mechanism for outside input into a federal decision.
